Kenya's geographic reference codes

Source: R/geographies.R
knbs_geographies.Rd

Returns the coded territorial hierarchy used by the 2019 Population and Housing Census: Kenya, its 47 counties, and their sub-counties, with names and parent codes. These are the join keys the census tables themselves use, read live from the same source (CC BY 4.0), never shipped as a snapshot that could drift from it.

Usage

knbs_geographies(
  level = NULL,
  vintage = NULL,
  parent = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  cache = knbs_option("cache"),
  refresh = FALSE
)

Arguments

level

Keep only these levels: "national", "county", "subcounty".

vintage

Reference frame year. Only 2019 is available; the argument exists so that code written today keeps meaning the same thing if other vintages arrive later.

parent

Keep only units whose parent_code is one of these, for example "01" for Mombasa's sub-counties.

source

Source id.

cache

Whether to use the local cache.

refresh

Whether to bypass any cached response.

Value

A knbs_geography tibble with columns geo_code, geo_name, geo_level, parent_code, parent_name, vintage and source_id.

Details

Codes are character and keep their leading zeros: "00" is Kenya, two digits are counties, four digits are sub-counties, and a sub-county's first two digits are its county. vintage is 2019 throughout — these are the census-frame units, and boundaries or units may have changed since. No other vintage, and no crosswalk to other coding systems, is offered, because none has been verified.

See also

knbs_get_indicator(), whose observations carry the same codes.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
counties <- knbs_geographies(level = "county")
knbs_geographies(parent = "01")
} # }
